task_name: The epic's branch: committed, pushed, never the default

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and the diff produces all three. (a) 'refusing before any write when that branch is the remote's default': GitEpicBranch#publish reads the branch with currentArgvFor, reads the remote's declaration with GitWorkspace.defaultBranchArgvFor + GitWorkspace.declaredBranchIn, and throws EpicBranchNotPublished before the first call to #add (git-epic-branch.ts:60-66). (b) 'commits the two documents': #add then #commit run in that order with the paths pathspec, which is what the brief asks for so that an untracked design document is staged first. (c) 'pushes it': #push runs ['-C', root, 'push', '--set-upstream', 'origin', branch] and publish answers the branch. Nothing the objective names is missing; the wiring of gate 1's press is tasks 5-6 and outside this **Files:** line.

The **TDD:** line names it('refuses before writing anything when the checkout sits on the branch the remote calls default') and fixes the assertion: rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD answers 'main', symbolic-ref answers 'refs/remotes/origin/main', it raises EpicBranchNotPublished and no add, commit or push was launched. The test in the diff (git-epic-branch.test.ts:145-157) arranges exactly those two answers (printing('main\n'), printing('refs/remotes/origin/main\n')), asserts toBeInstanceOf(EpicBranchNotPublished) and then asserts git.calls.some(argv => argv.includes('add'|'commit'|'push')) is false for each of the three. Same input, same assertion, same expected value. Its pair on 'epic/the-loop' (line 159) reaches all three calls, as the same line requires.

Name by name against the three Contract blocks and the Current state block. Port: class EpicBranch with current(root: CheckoutRoot): Promise<string> and publish({ root, paths, message }): Promise<string>, both throwing 'must implement', as in the named exemplar domain/ports/pull-requests.ts. Adapter: GitEpicBranch extends EpicBranch, static readonly REMOTE = 'origin', currentArgvFor(root), addArgvFor(root, paths), commitArgvFor(root, message, paths), pushArgvFor(root, branch), constructor({ run }: { run: ToolLaunch }) — parameter names and order as written. The four argv literals match the brief character for character, including the '--' separators and '--set-upstream'. add runs before commit. Current state: the matched line left GitWorkspace#declaredBase and is now the public static declaredBranchIn(printed): string | null (git-workspace.ts:176-179), which #declaredBase calls, and which GitEpicBranch reads together with the public GitWorkspace.defaultBranchArgvFor(root). exceptions.ts gains EpicBranchNotPublished and EpicBranchNotUnderstood under SpecFreezeFailure, and PlanCollapse gains 'epic-branch-not-published' and 'epic-branch-not-understood', kebab-case as backend/conventions/this-repository.md requires.

Row by row, the diff bears on three and reopens none. D-10 (everything new under backend/ is TypeScript): both new modules are .ts and use only erasable syntax. D-16 (cmux leaves the backend): no module in the diff names cmux. D-23 (after the freeze the app pushes the epic's branch and opens its pull request): the diff supplies the push half and touches nothing about merging, and D-7 (no write to a pull request, no merge button) is untouched — GitEpicBranch's argv list ends at push. D-11, D-13, D-18, D-21, D-22 have no subject in this diff: it adds no second opinion about freezability, stores no phase, and adds no endpoint a session could call.

Exemplars: the port copies domain/ports/pull-requests.ts (a class whose methods throw `${this.constructor.name} must implement ...` quoting what it was asked); the adapter copies infrastructure/git-workspace.ts (static argv builders, `asked.failed` read as data, the two typed causes); the test copies __tests__/infrastructure/git-workspace.test.ts down to the GitDouble shape — a class of named constants, an `answering(argv)` dispatch and a `calls` log. Rules read: plugin/conventions/* (all eight), backend/conventions/this-repository.md, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, .agent/conventions-ack.md; frontend/README.md does not bear (no frontend file). The skill backend-engineering:backend-best-practices loaded: it is a router to Python/Django references and its own precedence rule yields to the project's conventions, which this-repository.md already ranks third — nothing in it bears on this diff. architecture.md: layer direction respected (domain/ports imports only a value-object type; infrastructure imports domain and its sibling adapter), one folder per kind of inhabitant, one concept per module, exceptions in the one catalogue file this-repository.md declares. domain.md: EpicBranch is a second port over git but the document licenses it — 'two ports that end up reaching the same system are one collaborator only if they ask it the same thing'; Workspace is asked to cut a slice's worktree, EpicBranch to publish the epic's documents. boundaries.md: the failure of git is data (`asked.failed`), the cap arrives injected as `run` and the adapter picks none, and the adapter is named after its implementation (GitEpicBranch), not after its port. decisions.md: the point of the extraction — what the remote's default branch is now lives once, in GitWorkspace.declaredBranchIn, and both callers ask it; the duplicated diagnostic wording between #declaredBase and #defaultBranchOf is the idiom of a boundary, which the document explicitly excludes ('the idiom of a boundary is not a rule'). Noted and not filed: GitEpicBranch.REMOTE = 'origin' repeats GitWorkspace.REMOTE = 'origin', but the Contract block of the brief prescribes that constant literally, no business change forces touching both, and git-workspace.ts already spells 'origin' in three places. style.md: no comments, English throughout, every function hangs off a type. defects.md, its four rules answered one by one: (1) closed vocabulary — the two new failures enter PlanCollapse's Projection keyed by the exception class, an exhaustive map with no catch-all branch, and no new boolean or hand-compared classifier is introduced; complies. (2) raw map as the return value of logic — none: publish and current answer a branch name (a string the Contract fixes), declaredBranchIn answers string | null, and no map crosses two of the diff's own functions; complies. (3) two fields that have to agree, sentinels included — none: the absence of a declared default is null in the type rather than an empty string, and current raises EpicBranchNotUnderstood when git printed nothing instead of answering ''; complies. (4) an error named for where it happens — EpicBranchNotPublished and EpicBranchNotUnderstood name what happened, inherit from SpecFreezeFailure rather than from the root PlanFailure, and split the family's two causes the way this-repository.md's 'Naming an exception family' asks; complies. Delivery: no document of either yardstick prescribes a shape of delivery for adding a port and its adapter, and this change alters no existing signature or public contract — GitWorkspace#declaredBase keeps its behaviour and its callers.

Does not apply: the diff's only '-' lines are two in backend/src/infrastructure/git-workspace.ts, production code, and they are the extraction the Current state block asks for (`const declared = asked.stdout.trim().match(GitWorkspace.#DECLARED)` becomes a call to `GitWorkspace.declaredBranchIn(asked.stdout)`, and `return declared[1]` becomes `return declared`). No test file loses a line: git-epic-branch.test.ts is new and no pre-existing test was touched, so no assertion, case or test was removed, relaxed or rewritten.

The promised behaviour lives in production code. The refusal is produced by `if (branch === declaredDefault) throw new EpicBranchNotPublished(...)` in src/infrastructure/git-epic-branch.ts, the three writes by #add/#commit/#push, and the argv the test compares against are built by the adapter's own static builders — the test's constants are the inputs and the expected literals, not the behaviour. Delete git-epic-branch.ts and every one of the four tests fails at import. The double intercepts only the external system (git) exactly at the ToolLaunch seam, which is where conventions/testing.md says an adapter is cut.

Inside the six declared files, every line traces to a sentence of the task. git-workspace.ts gains only declaredBranchIn and the two lines of #declaredBase that now call it — the Current state block's instruction, and no other behaviour of that module moves. start-plan-route.ts gains only the two imports and the two Projection rows the brief's last contract sentence asks for. exceptions.ts gains exactly the two classes named. No refactor, rename or adjacent fix rides along; nothing under plugin/scripts, plugin/skills or frontend/ is touched, and nothing the **Out of scope** list names by name (the groom, analyzeSlicesTable, the merge, POST /start-plan's behaviour, creating the epic's branch) is altered — publish pushes the branch the checkout is already on and creates none. The diff contains no hunk of the plan file, so there is no amendment to justify.

Four new tests in backend/__tests__/infrastructure/git-epic-branch.test.ts, measured on the three properties. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no network, no filesystem, no randomness and no sleep — every git answer is a ProcessOutput the test constructs. Isolated: each test builds its own GitEpicBranchDouble with its own `calls` array; nothing module-level is mutated and no test depends on the order of the file. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are on what the adapter sent to the tool seam (the three literal argv arrays), on what publish returned ('epic/the-loop', 'feat/42') and on which exception class came out — all produced by src/infrastructure/git-epic-branch.ts, which is why reverting it turns all four red. The finer half was measured with control-tower-loop:test-driven-development, which loaded: nothing in it or in the double contradicts it — the double is not a mock asserted on its own call count but the scripted external system conventions/testing.md prescribes for an adapter, it raises when nobody wrote an answer for a request, and the fourth test's two halves are the 'both failure causes told apart' that the same document requires rather than two behaviours smuggled into one test. One observation not worth a finding: the second test pins the three argv arrays with toContainEqual, so it does not pin that `add` runs before `commit`, which is the reason the brief gives for the order; the test's name promises no order, so the assertion still matches its name.
